title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: Efficient antenna sensitization of Eu(III) or Tb(III) requires a ligand triplet roughly 2500–3000 cm^-1 above the accepting Ln excited level so ligand-to-metal energy transfer occurs without strong back-transfer.
explanation: Hard O/N donors (β-diketonates, Schiff bases, polyaminocarboxylates, carboxylates, phosphine oxides) provide both high molar absorptivity and stable chelation. After S0→Sn absorption, internal conversion and intersystem crossing populate T1, which is the usual donor; S1-to-Ln transfer can also operate when the gap allows it. A too-small gap, as when the hfa triplet lies close to Tb 5D4, suppresses emission by back-transfer.
scope: Mononuclear, polynuclear, polymer, and MOF Ln(III) complexes that rely on organic antenna ligands, illustrated especially for Eu(III) and Tb(III).
conditions: Typical path is ligand S0→Sn, IC to S1, ISC to T1, then energy transfer to Ln(III).
caveats: The 2500–3000 cm^-1 window is given as an example for Eu(III) or Tb(III), not a universal gap for every Ln ion. Exchange and resonance pathways can operate together.
evidence_locations: Section 3.3; Figs. 6–7; Section 5.2 pybox/hfa Tb discussion; refs. 44, 46, 53–67, 127
